decisions.decision: What uses bootstrap's git:* tasks?
decisions.ruling: Amended 2026-11-18 (D36, D37): land.mjs too: open calls git:worktree:create, close rebases its own branch (D37) and calls git:merge:<b>, then removes the worktree with git:worktree:delete, which also deletes the branch once it is merged and keeps it on a PR result (D35). git-workflow's landings call git:merge:<b> and git:worktree:create/setup/delete. The main checkout's uncommitted changes stay uncommitted and are never part of the merge (D23).
decisions.rejected: Prose landings only; land.mjs keeps its own merge and stash code.

decisions.decision: The core-branch rulings parked for R3 (docs/memory/gaps/2026-11-14-one-or-two-core-branches-parked.md), restated against the contract.
decisions.ruling: The integration branch is develop when develop is in repo.core_branches (bootstrap config get repo.core_branches --json), else main. With both, work moves feature → develop → main; with one, each feature lands on that branch. A core branch that exists only on origin gets a local branch that tracks origin/<branch>. The user's words: "If there's a develop branch then make changes on develop branch only and keep remote in sync so that other contributors don't run the same plan on their machine. In case develop branch does not exist and main does then use main with same rules". init gets two CONTRIBUTING.md variants (two branches, one branch). The pipeline seed shows each repo's core branches with a preselected stage/prod pair, and the user confirms. Doctor: the forge default branch is drift only when it names a branch that is not a core branch or does not exist.

decisions.decision: Stated by the planner, confirmed at the shape gate: the landing model.
decisions.ruling: git-workflow reads bootstrap config get repo.branches.<b>.landing --json: pr, direct-merge or direct-commit (R1a D11, D17). read_merge_model and every merge_model or [branch.*] name go. The git:merge:<b> task applies the model itself; git-workflow reads it only to tell the user what a landing will do and to refuse a direct commit where the value is not direct-commit.

decisions.decision: Stated by the planner, confirmed at the shape gate: land.mjs abandon.
decisions.ruling: Amended 2026-11-18 (D36, D43): abandon discards only land.mjs's own scratch. When the branch was made by open (open records its base in the branch config, branch.<name>.vwfLandBase) and every commit after that base carries close's trailer Vwf-Land: close, abandon removes the worktree with git worktree remove --force and the branch with git branch -D, dirty or unmerged. Otherwise it runs mise run git:worktree:delete -- <branch>; on exit 1 it keeps what is left and returns { abandoned: true, branch } with a warning that holds the task's output and the git branch -D command.

decisions.decision: Round 1 gap 2: the git:merge task prints plain text; how does close tell a merge from a PR or a conflict?
decisions.ruling: close reads the result from git after the task. Exit 0 with the branch merged into <into> (git merge-base --is-ancestor) is landed. Exit 0 with the branch not merged is a PR, with its URL from gh pr view <branch> --json url when gh is present, else no URL. A non-zero exit is failed, with the end of the task's output as the reason. The hooks-to-PR fallback and the push retry of land.mjs go: the task decides those.
decisions.rejected: Parse the task's text; add --json to the bootstrap task.

decisions.decision: Round 1 gap 3: a new refused kind breaks the JSON results that queue.mjs and start.mjs handle.
decisions.ruling: No new kind. A failed task, a dirty main checkout included, is the kind failed with the task's message. This replaces the refused result of U1's first ruling.
decisions.rejected: A new refused kind.

decisions.decision: Round 1 gap 4: finish is not ruled.
decisions.ruling: Amended 2026-11-18 (D36, D44, D48): finish deletes the local branch with git branch -D only when gh pr view <branch> --json state gives MERGED or glab mr view <branch> --output json gives the state merged. When it does, and the branch is land.mjs's own scratch (the D43 test), it also deletes origin/<branch> with git push origin --delete <branch>; it never deletes any other remote branch. With neither CLI, or another state, it keeps the branch and returns { finished: false, reason, command } with exit 1. It keeps git pull --ff-only of <into> when the main checkout is on <into>.
decisions.rejected: git:worktree:delete.

decisions.decision: Round 2 gap 1: on a conflict, git:merge exits 1 and leaves the main checkout mid-merge (bootstrap merge, about line 386); queue.mjs:467 needs the conflict kind.
decisions.ruling: Amended 2026-11-18 (D37): close never aborts a merge in the main checkout. A conflict of the branch with origin/<into> shows at the D37 rebase in close's own worktree, which returns the kind conflict. When the git:merge task exits non-zero and MERGE_HEAD exists in the main checkout, close collects the files (git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U) and returns failed, with a reason that names the files, says the main checkout is left mid-merge as the task left it, and gives the two ways out: resolve and commit, or git merge --abort.

decisions.decision: Round 2 gap 2: the task merges locally, then its push fails, leaving an unpushed merge commit on <into>.
decisions.ruling: Amended 2026-11-18 (D38): close does not reset <into>. After a non-zero exit with <into> ahead of the tip that close recorded before the task, close returns failed with a reason that says the merge commit stays on local <into>, not pushed, and that the next landing pushes it.

decisions.decision: Round 2 gap 3: --from origin/<into> needs a remote.

If it exits 1 and gh pr view <branch> --json state gives MERGED, or glab mr view <branch> --output json gives merged, run the git branch -D command that the task printed. Otherwise report the failure, a stale local core branch among its causes, and stop.

decisions.decision: Amend 2026-11-18, Q1 (bootstrap docs/sync/vwf.md:88 says plugins run git actions through the git:* tasks, not raw git; the plan kept destructive raw git: abandon and finish delete branches, finish also on origin with no merge check, and close aborts a merge, resets <into> and checks out again).
decisions.ruling: land.mjs runs no destructive raw git. abandon uses git:worktree:delete and keeps an unmerged branch (D5). finish deletes the local branch only when gh reports the pull request MERGED, and never deletes the remote branch (D11). close aborts no merge (D15, D37), resets nothing (D16, D31, D38) and checks nothing out after the task (D24). git branch --unset-upstream stays (D25, D30): it changes only the branch config. git-workflow's prose follows the same rule (D27).
decisions.rejected: Keep the destructive steps as D5, D11, D15, D16, D24 and D31 ruled; remove only finish's.

decisions.decision: Amend 2026-11-18, Q2: with no merge abort, a lost claim (another session changed the same row of docs/plans/index.json first) would leave the main checkout mid-merge on <into>, and every later landing would stop.
decisions.ruling: Before the git:merge task, close fetches (with an origin) and rebases its own branch on origin/<into> in its own worktree. A rebase conflict runs git rebase --abort in that worktree only, and returns the kind conflict with the conflicted files, so queue.mjs's lost result works unchanged. With no origin, close rebases on <into>. A conflict of the task in the main checkout can then come only from the user's own commits on local <into>, and is failed per D15.
decisions.rejected: Stop and report every lost claim; abort the merge in the main checkout only when MERGE_HEAD is close's own branch and the only conflicted file is docs/plans/index.json.

decisions.decision: Amend 2026-11-18: the reset of D16 and D31 is a destructive step (D36).
decisions.ruling: Amended 2026-11-18 (D45): checked after D15. When the task exits non-zero, MERGE_HEAD is absent, and the branch is in local <into> (git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> <into>) but not in origin/<into>, the push failed: close returns failed, the merge commit stays on local <into>, not pushed, and the next landing pushes it.
decisions.rejected: git reset --keep to the recorded tip.

decisions.decision: Amend 2026-11-18, Q3: the git:merge task merges with --no-edit, so the merge commit takes git's default subject; land.mjs can no longer give it --message, and plan-queue.test.ts:447 expects the merge subject to be the message.
decisions.ruling: The merge commit keeps git's default subject until bootstrap's git:merge task takes a message flag (Parked). close's --message is the subject of the change commit only, and the tests check the change commit's subject.
decisions.rejected: Git's default subject with no follow-up; rewrite the merge commit after the task (a force push).

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 1, gaps 1 and 2: abandon also discards land.mjs's own scratch worktrees (vwf-claim-<plan>, vwf-complete-<plan>, vwf-approve-<name>), which a retry opens again under the same name; a kept branch blocks the retry, and git:worktree:delete cannot remove a dirty worktree.
decisions.ruling: abandon may delete a worktree and its branch, dirty or unmerged, only when both are land.mjs's own: open records the base in branch.<name>.vwfLandBase, close adds the trailer Vwf-Land: close to each change commit, and abandon checks that every commit after the recorded base carries it (a branch with no commit qualifies). It then uses git worktree remove --force and git branch -D. Anything else is kept and reported (D5).
decisions.rejected: A unique branch name per attempt with everything kept; keep everything and stop the retry.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 1, gap 6: finish and D27 accepted only gh's MERGED, while D9 accepts a request opened by glab, or none when neither CLI exists.
decisions.ruling: finish and D27 accept gh pr view --json state MERGED or glab mr view --output json state merged. With neither CLI, finish keeps the branch and returns the git branch -D command for the user to run once they see the merge.
decisions.rejected: Also accept git ancestry of the branch tip in origin/<into> when no CLI exists.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 1, gaps 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9, stated by the planner and accepted by the user.
decisions.ruling: (3) On conflict or failed, close keeps the worktree for its caller, which retries or abandons it; it removes the worktree only on landed or PR. (4) close commits everything before the task, so the test of a failing task uses a stub hook of the safety net that fails, which gives failed. (5) The unstage git reset --quiet after a failed commit stays: it changes only the index; U1's verification grep looks for reset --keep and reset --hard. (7) close checks MERGE_HEAD (D15) before the failed push (D38). (8) Every failed reason after the task says that the task left the main checkout on <into>. (9) The task's whole-tree hook pass gates every claim, approval and completion, and a hook failure anywhere is failed (D23); U6's docs say so.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 2, gap 3: after a failed push (D38) the merge commit is only on local <into>; a retry of the same claim, completion or approval conflicts with it and leaves the main checkout mid-merge (D15).
decisions.ruling: close's D38 result carries the field unpushed: true beside kind failed (no new kind, D10), and its reason gives the command git push origin <into>, run from the main checkout. Every caller (queue.mjs, start.mjs, execute/references/land.md, plan-index.md, protected-branch.md) stops on it and reports it, and never retries it. A caller retries a conflict only.
decisions.rejected: land.mjs pushes local <into> before the retry, which also pushes the user's own unpushed commits.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 2, gaps 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7, stated by the planner and accepted by the user.
decisions.ruling: (1) After the D37 rebase, close records the new base again in branch.<name>.vwfLandBase, so a scratch branch stays abandonable (D43). (2) A failed reason says the main checkout is now on <into> only when close sees the main checkout's HEAD on <into> after the task; this replaces D45 (8). (4) A failed open throws LandError (exit 2, the message on stderr), as today; a failed finish returns { finished: false, reason, command } with exit 1. (5) U2 also owns execute/references/land.md (about line 45 aborts a merge; about line 60 runs finish), plan/SKILL.md (about line 570) and change-plan/references/hand-off.md (about line 37), and applies D15, D36, D44 and D46 there. (6) The one-branch variant is init/assets/hygiene/CONTRIBUTING-one-branch.md; init copies the chosen variant to the target repo as CONTRIBUTING.md. (7) U1's test edits also name git-land.test.ts about line 179, which expects the merge subject (D39).

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 3, gap 3: under the pr landing the git:merge task pushes the scratch branch to origin; finish never deleted a remote branch, and D26 refuses open while origin/<name> exists, so the next attempt under the same scratch name stops.
decisions.ruling: finish also deletes origin/<name>, only when gh or glab reports the request merged and the branch is land.mjs's own scratch (D43). It never deletes another remote branch.
decisions.rejected: open's refusal tells the user to delete origin/<name>; a unique scratch name per attempt.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 3, gaps 1, 2, 4 and 5, stated by the planner and accepted by the user.
decisions.ruling: (1) scripts/src/check.ts INIT_ROOT_ALLOWLIST (about lines 322-326) refuses CONTRIBUTING-one-branch.md: U3 owns scripts/src/check.ts and scripts/src/check.test.ts and adds the file to the list with a test; U6 updates the allowlist text of .claude/skills/plugin-authoring/references/checks.md. (2) When the task exits non-zero, MERGE_HEAD is absent and the branch is in origin/<into> (or, with no origin, in local <into>), the change landed and only the task's restore checkout failed (merge library about lines 415-425): close returns landed with a warning that holds the task's output. (3) git-workflow makes a worktree with git:worktree:create -- <name> --from origin/<into> --no-setup after a fetch (--from <into> with no origin), then git branch --unset-upstream when the branch has an upstream, and its Step 2c runs git:worktree:setup; U2 also edits worktree-setup.md about line 62 and git-workflow SKILL.md about lines 28 and 148. (4) bootstrap's merge refuses every landing into main from a branch other than develop while a develop branch exists, locally or on origin, and [branches.main] sets neither merge_from nor merge_never (merge library about lines 216-221), even when develop is not a core branch. Doctor's (g) reports a develop branch in a one-branch repo as drift, with the fix: delete develop, or set merge_from on main. U4 owns it.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 4, seven gaps, shown to the user after the fourth round; each ruling proposed by the planner and accepted by the user. No fifth round.

(2) The git merge <integration branch> of an all run's shared worktree (execute/references/setup.md about lines 89-93) runs in the run's own worktree, not the main checkout, so its git merge --abort stays; U2 also owns setup.md and states that rule there without citing land.md. (3) git-workflow SKILL.md step 4 (about lines 264-271) stops on a conflict and leaves the merge for the user, as D15; it runs no git merge --abort. (4) open writes branch.<name>.vwfLandBase before it calls git:worktree:create; when create fails, open removes what create left through the D43 scratch path, then throws LandError. (5) close refuses before the task, as failed, when the main checkout already has MERGE_HEAD, and says the main checkout was mid-merge before the landing. (6) U6 rewrites the landing-model lines of CLAUDE.md (about lines 310-316) and .claude/docs/ci-and-releases.md (about lines 38-42) to repo.branches.<b>.landing in .config/bootstrap/repo.toml; only the lines on the release tasks stay.
